rawItems.title: We visited bird sanctuary in Cambridgeshire and here’s what we thought
rawItems.content: Ben Jolley reports back from a visit to The Raptor Foundation in Woodhurst, Cambridgeshire It’s more important than ever to support local attractions - especially ones that are making a real difference. A registered charity for over 30 years and situated at its current site for the same amount of time, visiting The Raptor Foundation is not only fun for all ages but you'll be supporting a crucial cause too. Having started its life in Ramsey St Mary, before moving to its current, bigger premises in the late 1990s, the sanctuary is home to around 170 birds of prey, including between 35 and 40 different species. The Buzzard Lawn (Image: Newsquest) As the majority of these have come from a rescue background, money spent (entry is very affordable at £8 for adults, £5 for children and free for under threes) goes towards rescuing, rehabilitating and then returning native birds of prey back to the wild. Open to the public all year round, and currently appealing for builders to help create new aviaries, time spent at the foundation is both exciting and educational. The bird of prey displays - which feature rare owls and falcons soaring overhead - are thrilling to watch. If you’re lucky, some may even decide to perch on the seat next to you, which takes the phrase up close and personal to a whole new level. Plans have been submitted to create a new residential traveller site for a family near Ramsey. The application, reference 26/01646/FUL, seeks permission to change the use of land on the south side of Middle Drove, Ramsey Heights, to accommodate four static caravans for residential use. The proposals also include parking for vehicles, space for two touring caravans and the construction of a brick and tile utility and day room for residents. Existing hardstanding at the site would be retained. Applicant Christopher Reilly is seeking permission for the development to provide a permanent home for his family, who are members of the Gypsy and Traveller community. rawItems.title: Three teenagers arrested as police investigate Hunts e-bike robbery
rawItems.content: Three teenagers have been arrested after an e-bike robbery in Huntingdonshire. Police were called to Alconbury Weald, near Huntingdon, at 8.48pm on Wednesday, October 21, with a robbery believed to have taken place around 50 minutes earlier. By midday on Thursday, October 22, after carrying out enquiries, officers arrested three males - an 18-year-old from Peterborough, a 17-year-old from Ramsey Heights and a 15-year-old from Peterborough - on suspicion of robbery. All three were released on bail until January 21. Cambridgeshire Police confirmed an investigation is ongoing. More advice about personal safety, including robbery, can be found on the force's dedicated personal safety information pages on the Cambridgeshire Constabulary website.

items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Amenities Committee (Agenda Full Council 10 September 2026): Approved £14,500 contract for drainage improvements across Spinningfield recreation ground, alongside installation of replacement inclusive swing sets in September.

items.title: Great Whyte Pedestrian Safety & Speed Limit Review
items.content: From Ramsey Town Council Minutes (Ramsey Communities Neighbourhood Plan Examiner Report August 2026): Council resolved to submit a formal request to Cambridgeshire County Council Highways for a 20mph speed zone and upgraded zebra crossing along Great Whyte, following resident traffic survey feedback.
